Bug_Title: BSHIFT: 32 bit int shifted by an amount not in the range -31..31 (ICAST_BAD_SHIFT_AMOUNT)
Bug_Details:
The code performs shift of a 32 bit int by a constant amount outside
the range -31..31.
The effect of this is to use the lower 5 bits of the integer
value to decide how much to shift by (e.g., shifting by 40 bits is the same as shifting by 8 bits,
and shifting by 32 bits is the same as shifting by zero bits). This probably isn't what was expected,
and it is at least confusing.
Bug_Explanation: The code performs a left shift operation on a 32-bit integer by a constant amount outside the range -31..31. Shifting a 32-bit integer by 32 (or any multiple of 32) results in no shift because only the lower 5 bits of the shift amount are considered. Hence, shifting by 32 is equivalent to shifting by 0, which is not the intended behavior.
Trigger_Explanation: The test cases 'testShiftBy32' and 'testShiftBy40' trigger the bug by performing a left shift operation by 32 and 40 respectively, which are outside the valid range for 32-bit integers. Shifting by 32 or any multiple results in no shift (equivalent to shifting by 0), which is not expected and demonstrates the bug.
